Brearley lists history teacher Mariel Isaacson with a PhD from the Graduate Center, CUNY.

basis: The CUNY dissertation and the history teacher's degree align, but the sources found do not connect that teacher or dissertation author to the Grace Church School reviewer. The shared name and Pittsburgh subject alone do not establish identity.

evidence.says: Michael Hawkins of Kent State University reviewed Hitler and America in March 2013.
The University of Akron library staff portal lists the 2013 review of Hitler and America under Mike Hawkins.
Michael Hawkins started his library career at the University of Akron and later moved to Kent State University, where he headed the map library.
Kent State map librarian Michael Hawkins earned a history BA in 2008 and a European history MA in 2010 at East Tennessee State University.
Michael Hawkins earned a UCLA history PhD in 2008 with the dissertation Co-Producing the Postcolonial and began teaching at UC Riverside in 2008.

basis: The review is listed by Akron's library staff, and the Kent librarian's career connects Akron to Kent. His 2008 BA and subsequent MA are a different educational trajectory from the dissertation author's 2008 UCLA PhD and teaching at Riverside; the identification of the reviewer with the librarian is inferred from the institutional records.

evidence.says: Michael McGuire of Salem State University reviewed A Rainbow Division Lieutenant in France for H-War in December 2017.
Michael McGuire, visiting instructor at Salem State, completed the Boston University history dissertation An Ephemeral Relationship in 2012.
Michael Courtney McGuire's Bismarck in Walhalla is listed as a University of Pennsylvania PhD dissertation from 1993.

basis: The Salem State reviewer is linked to a 2012 Boston University history doctorate, while the other key's Bismarck dissertation is a 1993 University of Pennsylvania doctorate. The distinct dissertations and doctoral careers support identifying two scholars.

evidence.says: Monica Fitzgerald reviewed A Great and Noble Scheme for H-NewEngland, credited to the history department at California State University, East Bay.
Saint Mary's lists Monica Fitzgerald's 2003 paper Drunkards & Fornicators on Meetinghouse Hill: Gender, Religion and Identity in an Early New England Town.
Saint Mary's says Monica Fitzgerald earned an MA in history from California State East Bay and a PhD in American history from UC Davis.

basis: The distinctive 2003 paper resembles the dissertation title, and its author earned a degree at the reviewer's institution. The sources do not establish that she was at East Bay in 2008 or directly link the review to the dissertation, so the evidence falls short of the required identity link.

evidence.says: The publisher attributes a review of Calypso Jews to Patrick Taylor of H-Caribbean.
York identifies its humanities professor as Patrick D M Taylor.
A dissertation bibliography lists Patrick Robinson Raylor for The Trans-Siberian Railroad and the Russian Revolution of 1905, Tennessee, 1969.

basis: The York reviewer's initials D M differ from the dissertation author's middle name Robinson. The bibliography transcribes the dissertation author's surname as Raylor, though its title and date match the graph record; the distinction is inferred from the names and affiliations.

evidence.says: Philip Rosen, born in 1928, was education director and curator of the Holocaust Museum in Cherry Hill from 1987 to 2001.
P. T. Rosen's The Politics of Broadcasting, 1920–1927 was a 1975 history doctoral dissertation at Wayne State University.
Smithsonian Libraries catalogs The Modern Stentors by Philip T. Rosen, born 1946.

basis: The Cherry Hill director was born in 1928. The dissertation is attributed to P. T. Rosen, consistent with the broadcasting historian Philip T. Rosen cataloged as born in 1946; the different birth years and careers support separate people.

evidence.says: Lists Richard John Ascarate as reviewer of A Concise History of Germany in H-Net in September 2005.
Credits Richard Ascarate of the U.S. Government Accountability Office with the March 2008 review of Overturning Dr. Faustus.

basis: The sources identify the two reviews but do not establish that their authors are the same person or link the two affiliations. Shared name and subject alone are insufficient for a merge.

evidence.says: Shannon Smith, professor at Saint Benedict and Saint John's, holds a Ph.D. from Indiana University.
Cites Shannon Smith, The Politics of Progress and the American-Russian Relationship, 1867–1917, as a Cornell University Ph.D. dissertation, 1994.

basis: The reviewer’s institutional profile identifies an Indiana doctorate, while the other key’s dissertation is a Cornell doctorate. These distinct doctoral careers strongly indicate two scholars.

evidence.says: Stephen Moore lists the 2021 H-War review and study at UC Riverside in 2018–2024, alongside a 2021 presentation on modern folk.
Stephen I. Moore's Modern Folk is a 2024 history PhD dissertation at the University of California, Riverside.
The book cites Stephen David Moore's Losing Minorca as a 2008 PhD dissertation at York University.

basis: The reviewer is linked to the Riverside doctoral career, while the author of Losing Minorca has a different middle name and a separate history doctorate at York. The distinct doctorates and names strongly indicate two people.

The review credits give University of Wales and University of Wales Aberystwyth in the same period, but the first credit does not identify a campus. No source found links the reviews or places the first reviewer at Aberystwyth.

evidence.says: Thomas Laub of Sweet Briar College reviewed The Rhineland 1945 for H-German in July 2005.
Thomas Laub, independent scholar, reviewed The Battle of the Bulge for H-German in July 2005.
Thomas Laub, independent scholar, reviewed War in the Wild East for H-German in October 2005.

basis: The reviews share a name and publication venue, but the sources found do not establish that the Sweet Briar reviewer and the independent scholar are the same person. The differing affiliations do not by themselves establish two people either.

evidence.says: The 2004 program lists Tuska Benes at the University of Pennsylvania.
The 2011 contributor note identifies Tuska Benes as associate professor of history at the College of William and Mary.

basis: The dated affiliations are compatible with the two review credits, but the sources found do not link the two sets of reviews or establish that the Pennsylvania and William and Mary scholars are one person.

evidence.says: Yi Sun lists both education articles, a BA in education in 2002, and a PhD in education in 2007, both at Beijing Normal University.
Washington State University reports Yi Sun defended the John Foster Dulles and China Dilemma history PhD thesis in August 1994.

basis: The author of both articles followed an undergraduate and doctoral education at Beijing Normal University from 1998 to 2007, whereas the thesis author defended a history doctorate at Washington State in 1994. These distinct educational timelines strongly indicate two people.

evidence.says: Julio Martínez-Cava Aguilar was a predoctoral researcher at the University of Barcelona and authored ‘Enemigo a las puertas’ in 2020.
Julio Martínez-Cava Aguilar submitted ‘Gorros frigios en la Guerra Fría’ for a doctorate in sociology at the University of Barcelona in 2020.
Julio Aguilar was a history doctoral candidate at UC Davis in 2021, writing ‘A Thirsty Colonization: Water and Urban Political Ecology in the Silver City of Potosí, 1573–1770’.

basis: The article author and the Potosí dissertation author had distinct doctoral careers at different universities in the same period. The university thesis and fellowship records support treating them as different scholars.

evidence.says: Steven Andrew King of Nottingham Trent University wrote ‘Remembering the Dead Poor in the Midlands, 1750s to 1880s’.
‘Women, Migration and Textile Work’ cites Steven King's 1993 Liverpool PhD thesis on demographic change in Calverley.
Steven William King wrote ‘Church and state relations in seventh century England’, a University of North Dakota Doctor of Arts dissertation awarded in 1998.

basis: The two works are credited to Steven Andrew King and Steven William King respectively, and the latter's North Dakota doctorate differs from the Liverpool PhD cited in the former's article. The distinct full names and doctoral records strongly indicate two scholars; the repository dates the second dissertation to 1998 rather than the item's 1997.

evidence.says: Daniel Moroni Stewart's education includes archaeology in 2006 and 2009 and history in 2016; his works include Social advancement (2021).
Daniel Moroni Stewart, ORCID 0000-0003-2466-7320, holds a doctorate in history from the University of Chile.
Cites Daniel Stewart's Temporary Samurai as a 2003 University of California, Berkeley PhD dissertation.

basis: The thesis on key b is a Berkeley doctorate, while the author on key a has a different history doctorate at the University of Chile and a separately documented education in archaeology. These distinct educational paths support two scholars; the conclusion is inferred rather than explicitly stated by a source.
